title_en: I Tried to Get a Six-Star Wanted Level in GTA 6 With Just One Bullet and Broke the Game
summary_en: We tried to get six stars in GTA 6 by firing just one bullet and broke the game.
body_en:
If reaching a six-star wanted level in Grand Theft Auto 6 is your goal, there are many different methods available to you. Raiding the military base for a tank is one way. Committing a horrifying beach massacre is another. But can you get there by firing just a single bullet? We at IGN had a theory that this was absolutely possible, and so spent hours in a fast food joint to find out.
When we say “by firing a single bullet,” we mean that technically speaking. Our theory is that your chosen character only needs to pull the trigger once. That’s because, when roaming around GTA 6’s open world and causing whatever brand of chaos you’ve chosen to, your partner will automatically take up the fight against aggressors, and is both invulnerable and stocked with unlimited ammunition. That means if you decide to walk into a heavily populated area as a couple and fire just one bullet into the crowd, your better half can commit the lion's share of the atrocities themselves, provided you just stay alive.
We tested this out for ourselves, leading Jason and Lucia to the Taco Bomb in Gellhorn as our chosen arena of violence. Taking control of Jason, one bullet was fired into a poor staff member taking a break outside. Bits of brain now covered the forecourt, which somehow still looked like a more appetising alternative to whatever the questionable-looking beef was they were offering inside. Creeping cannibalistic thoughts pushed to one side, we walked back inside knowing our work was done. This public execution, perhaps rightfully, attracted a police patrol car to the restaurant, of which Lucia did not take kindly to their arrival.
Her love for Jason knows no bounds, up to and including unloading full machine gun magazines into any cops who want to arrest him. And who were we to stand in her way? Letting her take control of the situation was then required, honorably moving Jason behind the indestructible cover of an industrial refrigerator. Sporting an armoured vest just in case any stray bullets or shrapnel found their way around the corner, it was then time to hunker down in the kitchen beside that thick metal fridge, out of view of law enforcement. Crucially, this fast food establishment’s kitchen does not have a door leading outside, meaning the threat of flanking cops was neutralised. Luckily, they didn’t seem to spot the drive-thru window, which would’ve handed them a clean shot.
And there we sat for a good 45 minutes as Lucia angrily gunned down anyone brave enough to step into the restaurant. No more food would be served today, only death. The red of discarded hot sauce packets replaced by the blood of the fallen. The crunch of hard shell tacos drowned out by the crack of broken bones. All in the name of science. Could a six-star wanted level be achieved by us, the player, firing just one bullet?
Well, not this time. We could’ve sat here forever, bravely hiding behind a fridge while our partner slaughtered hundreds. Lucia was invincible, rounds of ammunition sinking into her skin to no effect. She had no shortage of ammo herself; with an unlimited pool of lead to reload from, she could’ve done this all day, and all for us. If that isn’t true romance, I don’t know what is. Day turned to night, and the restaurant workers diligently remained kneeling behind the counter and cowering for the whole sordid ordeal.
The problem is, our aggressors just… stopped. After a period of quiet, we chose to break cover and wander outside, only to be met by several non-aggravated members of law enforcement staring blankly at us. We had seemingly confused them with our methods of madness.
Because we’re so dedicated to the cause here at IGN, we tried all over again. Putting this first attempt down as an unfortunate glitch, we reloaded a save, made our way to Taco Bomb, and fired a single gunshot into our chosen test subject. And so, another hour of hiding behind a fridge commenced while our incredibly committed girlfriend peppered anyone who dared approach us with bullets. Armoured trucks eventually surrounded the exits, and the sound of helicopter blades could be heard above. But the same thing happened again. We even waited long enough for the rest mode settings on our PS5 to almost put the console to sleep.
It seems GTA 6 gets very confused if you decide to start a chain reaction like this, only to go passive for the next 60 minutes. Again, five stars were secured on the wanted level, but that sixth just wouldn’t arrive. The enemy AI’s brain could not comprehend what was happening, so we decided we simply had to intervene. If that sixth star was going to be ours, we’d need to get involved ourselves.
Thus, we thought we’d honor the place we’d called home for the past couple of hours, and end our occupancy of Taco Bomb with an explosion. A bunch of incapacitated, but not dead, cops lay writhing on the floor of the restaurant. Could just one grenade be our key to maxing out the wanted level? There was only one way of finding out. We ended the whole bloody affair with a bang, ripping the pin out of the explosive before hurling it into the mound of bodies. And that’s when it happened. Nirvana. The gates of heaven opened. Six-star paradise was ours to bask in.
So, what was the point of all of this? Well, more than anything, to confirm that you never have to worry about Jason or Lucia dying when roaming around GTA 6’s open world when not controlling them. Unlike in missions, where they can slip off this mortal coil, they can’t die in free-roam, and so you are clear to use them as superpowered distractions or unkillable meat shields if you wish. You don’t have to be as cowardly as we were, but if you have an hour free to watch an action movie scene play out while peeking out from behind the corner of a refrigerator, then that option is available to you.
There are certainly quicker ways to reach GTA 6’s highest wanted level of six stars, which means you’ll be hunted down until you’re dead, but this is one of the safest and requires minimal munitions from your own stockpile. Early on, we opted for the plane crash onto a beach, before mowing down all of the vacationers in a truck method, but since then, millions of players have been finding their own road to infamy.
But, in case you ever needed to know. Yes, it is possible to get six stars in GTA 6 with just a single bullet and grenade. As for just the single bullet itself… well, we’ll keep on trying.
What have been your wildest six-star stories? Let us know in the comments!
